Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup,InnerProductSpace R,FiniteDimensional R,MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical full-space volume,including dimension zero. Let V:E->R,alpha,beta:NNReal,eta:R. Assume alpha cast>0,alpha<=beta,V C2 and for EVERY x,a:E BOTH actual bounds
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define the actual measures,potential and CLM-valued function
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta),
  s_y(z)=-(1/2)*fderiv R V ((y+z)/2)-(1/(4*eta))*innerSL R (y-z).
For each direction a:E this is the real directional function
  q_{y,a}(z)=s_y(z)[a]=-(1/2)*(fderiv R V ((y+z)/2) a)-<y-z,a>/(4*eta).
It is the formula-defined unnormalized PARAMETER-y directional score,not a centered normalized score or the negative z-gradient. Tilt,Gaussian,independent product and pushforward are actual measures.
There exist common kernels R,S:E->Measure E with both Markov,R a true conditional kernel disintegrating J.map Prod.swap,and for EVERY y,S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For EVERY y,S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)),W_y C2,exp(-W_y) volume-integrable and its volume integral strictly positive. For this y there exists ONE original real-linear partial operator D:Lp R 2 (S(y))->partialLinear[R] Lp E 2 (S(y)),with dense domain in scalar L2,D closable,D.closure closed,and exact graph: for every scalar L2 b/vector L2 G,(b,G) is in D.graph iff exists smooth compactly supported real phi with b=phi S(y)-AE and G=gradient(phi) S(y)-AE.
This SAME D has the following centered-domain inequality: for EVERY z:D.closure.domain with integral (z as scalar representative)(x) dS(y)(x)=0,
  ((alpha+1/eta)/4)*||z as scalar L2(S(y))||^2 <= ||D.closure(z)||^2.
Furthermore for EVERY direction a:E,ALL three assertions hold:
  Integrable q_{y,a} (S(y)),
  Integrable (z->(q_{y,a}(z)-integral q_{y,a}(x) dS(y)(x))^2) (S(y)),
  Integrable (z->||gradient(q_{y,a})(z)||^2) (S(y)),
and the actual directional-score variance is bounded by
  integral (q_{y,a}(z)-integral q_{y,a}(x) dS(y)(x))^2 dS(y)(z)
  <= (1/eta-alpha)^2/(4*(alpha+1/eta))*||a||^2.
The three integrability conditions exactly expand Admissible(S(y),q_{y,a});the variance is the literal centered-square integral using that same S(y),with no prefactor or division by measure mass. gradient q is exactly the real Riesz representative of fderiv R q. All alpha occurrences in real formulas are NNReal-to-real casts.
One common R,S pair precedes ALL y;one original D per y precedes ALL centered-domain z and ALL score directions a. They are existential common-law witnesses,not identified with project-owned canonical selected kernels. Density/operator conclusions hold every y;conditional disintegration has standard version scope without claiming these identities for every possible conditional version. No alternate D or equality of two distinct conditional kernels is added.
Partition integrals use volume;mean/variance/Admissible/norm inequality use actual S(y). No score mean-zero premise or conclusion is inserted:variance centers the unnormalized score by its actual mean. No separate C1/gradient-bound/score-domain-pair assertion beyond displayed conclusions is added from older packets. This exact scalar fiberwise domain/score-variance result does not assert normalized-score differentiation,marginal Poincare,Hessian-inverse anisotropic inequality,rough Hessian or a main/cost composition theorem,or joint measurable fiber selection.
